title: Reject a single-release guarantee reused on a correlated block
statement: The one-use all-reference budget does not supply the same constant for arbitrary correlated repeated inputs. The source gives an explicit repetition counterexample. Independent exact tickets for a single raw-input release and a physical/stochastic calibration warrant do not turn that theorem into composable disclosure security.

requires: Strictly positive column-stochastic square invertible rationalL; positiveKentry floor and specified output alphabet
Exact conditional/equal-reference entropy semantics with defined finite differences; all finite quantum references
Actual raw classical input X, independent exact random tickets and supplied utility/budget
provides: The one-use all-reference budget does not supply the same constant for arbitrary correlated repeated inputs. The source gives an explicit repetition counterexample. Independent exact tickets for a single raw-input release and a physical/stochastic calibration warrant do not turn that theorem into composable disclosure security.
assumptions: The input is supplied rationalL and raw classicalX, not already-noisy data, an unknown physical reference or acquired private source. ApplyingK needs independent private randomness. One-use information comparison is not differential privacy, guessing/Blackwell dominance, adaptive disclosure security or a correlated-block budget. The nominal-to-actual margin additionally needs a simultaneous deterministic entry-error promise; finite fitted calibrations do not acquire it. Ordinary stronger comparators, failed initial proposal, solver/bit costs and no practical advantage remain.
costs: Finite rational inverse/covariance and exact semidefinite certificate/ticket processing
Weak optimization, rational heights/precision and actual input access/randomness/calibration costs; nominal theorem is not physical privacy
